one_line: Per-object revocable authority for agent writes, allowing one sensitive item to be held while other work continues.

leverage_rationale: Per-object revocation changes the collaboration model: the agent can keep working on shared state while one object is withdrawn, which is not comparably expressible through ordinary UI clicking or coarse global approval switches.
leverage_evidence: Core concept is object-by-object authority with live revocation.
Description says held objects are communicated through the structured tool channel and cannot be overridden.
Two frame sheets are submitted, though the available inspected frame showed DevTools and no legible invocation details.
execution_rationale: The interaction model is coherent and the packet provides substantial conceptual detail plus video frame sheets, but the small contact-sheet evidence does not clearly prove the complete flow.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show a loaded application with repeated UI states and DevTools open.
Written description defines HOLD, reject/cut, and whole-board lock behaviors.
Demo is reported alive and public repository exists.
impact_rationale: Fine-grained authority is valuable anywhere agents edit sensitive shared artifacts, from contracts to code and budgets; the need is concrete and broadly reusable.
impact_evidence: Examples include deal terms, repo files, config keys, PR hunks, and budget lines.

usability_note: The three-move control model is simple in concept and preserves agent momentum.

standouts: Highly differentiated interaction model.

one_line: Privacy-preserving in-browser analysis of large sensitive files without exposing raw rows to an agent.
what_it_does: Grades and seals columns, exposes bounded statistical tools, refuses identifying or exact-value queries, and records the bytes returned to the agent.
leverage_rationale: The product depends on in-page structured tools and controlled data boundaries: the agent can direct analysis of data it cannot address or receive, a capability that disappears without WebMCP rather than merely becoming less convenient.
leverage_evidence: Description reports 98.9 MB read in-browser, 2.2 KB released, and zero raw rows.
Tools are withdrawn and re-registered when a column is sealed.
Eight bounded tools omit run_sql and refuse exact salary extraction.
execution_rationale: The packet contains a detailed 145-second transcript and three frame sheets describing a coherent end-to-end workflow, privacy guardrails, recovery behavior, and network isolation; the visual contact sheets are low-resolution but the evidence package is unusually complete.
execution_evidence: 145-second video is reported with transcript covering analysis, refusal, charting, receipts, and exfiltration tests.
Transcript describes five blocked network paths and a one-second query claim at large scale.
Demo and public source are reported available.
impact_rationale: Organizations with sensitive large datasets have a real need for useful analysis without uploading or disclosing rows; the demonstrated privacy boundary directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Use case covers salaries and identifying columns.
Agent receives aggregate results and charts but no raw rows or names.
Human can override column sealing and inspect a byte-level receipt.
creativity_rationale: The capability split—agent-directed analysis with zero row disclosure, dynamic tool revocation, and explicit refusal alternatives—is novel and pursued at substantial technical depth.
creativity_evidence: In-page analysis avoids the usual server-side MCP data custody problem.
Privacy constraints are part of the tool contract and interaction design, not a disclaimer.
usability_note: Refusals provide legal statistical alternatives and the receipt makes the boundary inspectable; the workflow is specialized but clear.
red_flags: Some security and scale claims remain dependent on the submitted demo rather than independent testing.
Contact sheets alone are not legible at individual-frame level.
standouts: WebMCP is genuinely indispensable to the claimed experience.
Strong privacy-by-construction interaction and auditability.
advance_reason: Top-tier leverage, impact, creativity, and unusually strong execution evidence.

one_line: An in-page trust layer that governs, confirms, limits, redacts, and audits WebMCP actions.

leverage_rationale: Security enforcement inside the page addresses the unique trust boundary created by WebMCP and can make otherwise unsafe agent actions governable; it is infrastructure for the agent surface rather than a UI convenience.

execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo reported.

impact_evidence: Targets agent shopping and human reluctance to allow payment completion.
Controls quantity, amount, session budget, PII exposure, and instruction injection.

red_flags: Payment and security claims are not independently verified in the packet.

standouts: WebMCP-native security model.

advance_reason: High-leverage infrastructure with substantial impact and ambitious safety mechanisms.
